summary: This is a controlled simulation study quantifying the finite-sample negative bias of the plug-in semantic-entropy (SE) estimator used in LLM uncertainty quantification, at the small-K (3-50) and small-alphabet-size (C=2-10) regimes actually used in practice. The core finding, unchanged since v1 and reproduced exactly by me from scratch, is that plug-in SE is negatively biased by 28-84% of its Miller-Madow-corrected value depending on K, that this bias is worst in the high-true-uncertainty (flat, large-C) regime where UQ matters most, and that the bias-correction has a large effect on absolute entropy values but essentially no effect on ranking (AUROC) at K<=5. This revision adds two reviewer-requested robustness checks (non-Dirichlet cluster-mass shapes; an entailment-clustering-noise model showing label noise can partially cancel the sampling bias and cause the MM correction to overshoot into positive bias at K=10/eps=0.2), and corrects a runtime figure flagged as wrong by the round-1 reviewer.
strengths:
- Full independent reproduction: I re-ran both experiment.py and experiment_v2.py from scratch (not just reading the logs) and every headline number in the paper's Table 1, per-regime bias values, AUROC ties/divergences, top-1 comparison numbers, bimodal/power-law robustness numbers, and the eps=0.2/K=10 MM-overshoot to +0.033 reproduced to the reported precision (deterministic sha256 seeding as claimed)
- The revision substantively responds to prior review rather than papering over it: it re-measured and corrected a previously wrong runtime claim (28.4s+27.0s -> the actual 213.8s+214.6s, which I independently confirmed is the right order of magnitude, my own runs took 220.0s and 220.5s), and regenerated the previously-missing run_log_v2.txt artifact
- The two new robustness experiments are genuine additions, not checkbox padding: the clustering-noise result (label noise partially cancels sampling bias and, combined with MM correction, can overshoot into positive bias at moderate K) is a non-obvious, mechanistically explained finding with real practical implications for when correction should not be applied blindly
- Appropriately scoped claims throughout: the paper is explicit that it is a simulation abstracting away real entailment clustering, explains why (TLS failure prevented model downloads), and repeatedly flags where its parametric choices (Dirichlet, bimodal, power-law, i.i.d. label-flip) are plausibility-motivated rather than fit to real data
weaknesses:
- The central contribution is an empirical quantification of a mechanically-expected, textbook fact (Miller-Madow bias, known since 1955) in a new but narrow parameter regime; no new estimator, theory, or methodology is proposed, and the 'why this matters' case rests on the assumption that practitioners are not already aware plug-in entropy is biased at low K, which is plausible but not demonstrated
- The paper still has no real LLM or entailment-model validation (fully disclosed as a limitation), so the practically important number for the reader -- how large is the clustering-noise rate epsilon actually is in production entailment pipelines -- is unknown; the eps=0.2 overshoot, the paper's most novel finding, is explicitly an 'existence proof, not a calibrated threshold,' which limits its actionability
- The C-range anchor (2-10) rests on a single cited paper (arXiv:2509.14478), and the shape/noise robustness sweeps, while broader than v1, are still parametric families chosen for plausibility rather than fit to measured cluster-mass or entailment-error distributions, so 'robust to non-Dirichlet shapes' should be read narrowly (robust across the shapes tried, not shapes in general)
questions:
1. Now that the runtime figure has been corrected and is stated as environment-dependent, is there still value in reporting a wall-clock number at all in the main text, versus moving it entirely to an appendix/artifact note?
2. Do the authors have any planned or in-progress access to a real entailment-clustering model (even a small NLI model, not requiring the blocked model-hub download) to get even a rough empirical estimate of eps, which would substantially strengthen the practical relevance of the overshoot finding?
3. For the 'ranking is robust, absolute value is not' conclusion, are there realistic LLM-UQ deployment settings where the absolute SE value (not just its rank) is the deciding factor for abstention, beyond the conformal-calibration use case already cited?
